# Get a Quick Summary of Unread Emails with Apple Mail's Priority Messages

> **In short:** Apple Mail uses Apple Intelligence to put important unread emails in a Priority section at the top of your inbox, with a short summary preview above each message. It works on iPhone 15 Pro and newer running iOS 18.1 or later, and the feature is free.

Open Apple Mail on the right kind of iPhone, iPad, or Mac, and the inbox looks different than it used to — the messages you actually want to read sit at the top, with a two-line summary telling you what each one wants before you tap in. By the end of this guide, you will have turned that on, learned where the priority section lives, and know how to read a summary in seconds. This one is aimed at complete beginners, so we will move slowly.

## Before you start
- An iPhone, iPad, or Mac that supports **Apple Intelligence** (Apple's built-in AI system that runs on the device). As of writing, that means iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max, every iPhone 16 model, any iPad with an **M1 chip or later** (the M1 is Apple's processor — the brain of the device — introduced in 2020), and any Mac with M1 or later.
- **iOS 18.1, iPadOS 18.1, or macOS Sequoia 15.1** or later. Check by opening Settings → General → Software Update.
- An Apple account with **Apple Intelligence turned on** in Settings (we do that in Step 1).
- About 5 minutes total.

## Step 1 — Turn on Apple Intelligence
Open the **Settings** app (the gray gear icon on your home screen). Scroll down and tap **Apple Intelligence & Siri** — if you don't see that exact wording, look for a section simply called **Apple Intelligence**. Tap the switch next to **Apple Intelligence** so it turns green. The system may take a few minutes to finish a one-time download in the background; you'll see a small spinning circle until it is done.

💬 Example: if a window pops up asking about sharing data, tap **"Use On-Device Processing"** so your emails stay private on the phone itself.

**If it looks different:** older devices won't show Apple Intelligence at all — that is the feature telling you the hardware is not supported, and no setting will bring it back. You will need a newer device to follow this guide.

You'll know it worked when the toggle stays green and Apple Intelligence appears in your **App Library** as a new icon, or simply as a finished download with no error message.

## Step 2 — Open Mail and look for the Priority section
Open the **Mail** app (the blue envelope icon). At the very top of your inbox, above your regular list of messages, look for a section labeled **Priority Messages**. It only shows up when there is at least one unread email Apple Intelligence thinks matters. The rest of your inbox — newsletters, receipts, promotional pings — stays below in their normal order.

💬 Example: when your unread inbox has three urgent messages and forty newsletters, you will see something like "Priority Messages (3)" pinned at the top, then all forty other emails underneath.

**If it looks different:** some users see the section labeled **"Priority"** instead of "Priority Messages." On older iOS versions you may not see it at all — update your software in Settings → General → Software Update.

You'll know it worked when the Priority section appears at the top with a small badge showing the count of priority unread emails.

## Step 3 — Read the summary at the top of a priority email
Tap one of the emails inside the Priority section to open it. Right below the sender's name and above the message body, Apple Intelligence adds a small block of text — usually two to four short lines — that summarizes what the message is asking, who it is from, and whether it needs a reply. Read that first.

💬 Example: for an email titled "Project review notes from yesterday," the summary might read: *"Maya shared three action items from the review meeting. She needs feedback by Thursday."* You now know the gist without scrolling past a wall of pasted meeting notes.

**If it looks different:** if you don't see a summary at all, swipe down on the email to refresh, then close and reopen it. Some very short emails don't get a summary because there is nothing to shorten.

You'll know it worked when a short paragraph appears in slightly bolded text right under the sender information, before the actual message starts.

## Step 4 — Tap to expand any full message you want
Read the summary, then decide. If the summary is all you needed, swipe down on the email or tap back to return to the inbox — you have just handled a message in seconds instead of minutes. If you want the full text, scroll past the summary box to read the original email underneath.

💬 Example: a short summary like *"Reminder: dentist appointment at 3pm"* tells you everything; you don't need to read further. A longer one like *"Sarah is asking for approval on the new design"* makes you want to scroll down and look at the attachment.

**If it looks different:** if Apple Intelligence thinks an email is sensitive (a password reset, a banking notification), it may hide the summary by default and show a small lock icon — tap that and authenticate with Face ID or your passcode.

You'll know it worked when you can decide in a glance whether each priority message deserves your full attention.

## Step 5 — Teach Mail what matters to you
Apple Mail decides what is "priority" mostly by watching which senders you actually open and reply to. You can speed this up. Open an email from someone you always want to see at the top, tap their name or photo at the top of the message, and choose **Add to VIP** from the menu. Their future emails will land in Priority automatically.

💬 Example: if your manager's messages keep showing up in the regular inbox instead of Priority, opening one of their emails and tapping their name → **Add to VIP** fixes that within a minute.

**If it looks different:** if you can't find "Add to VIP," tap the sender's email address under their name — Apple's menus move around between iOS versions and you may need to tap a small ⓘ (info) symbol first.

You'll know it worked when VIP senders appear at the very top of your inbox, before Priority, and their future messages always count toward the priority badge.

## Common mistakes
- **Looking for Priority on the wrong device.** It only works on supported hardware running iOS 18.1 or later. On older iPhones or iPads, the section simply does not exist — that is not a setting you are missing.
- **Assuming Apple Intelligence learned your habits in a day.** The first week the system is on, the Priority section may feel random. After roughly a week of normal use, the picks get much sharper.
- **Ignoring the summary out of caution.** The summary lives on your device and does not send your email anywhere. If you do not trust a particular email, do not act on the summary — open the full message instead, just like before.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** instead of scrolling past 200 newsletters every morning to find the one email that matters, your three most important messages are waiting at the top of Mail the moment you open the app, already half-read.
- **For your business or work:** triage (deciding which emails need attention first) takes about a minute. You read the three priority summaries, decide which to open fully, and leave the rest for later.
- **If you're just getting started:** do Steps 1 and 2 only. Open Mail tomorrow morning and see how many real unread emails were already at the top — that alone will save you noticeable time.

## Try it now
Open Mail right now, scroll to the top of your inbox, and read just the summaries of any priority emails for 60 seconds. Mark one you don't need as read and move on. That single pass is the whole workflow in miniature.
